what: The readlist says that writing `mod stock;` a second time 'would build two different rooms'. A real run shows otherwise: a second `mod stock;` in another file looks under that file's folder and fails with E0583. That failure is the exact case the compiler note quoted on this panel describes.
evidence: Page: "Writing mod stock; twice would build two different rooms." My scratch run (rustc 1.99.1: src/stock.rs exists; main.rs has `mod stock; mod other;`; other.rs has `pub mod stock;`) printed: "error[E0583]: file not found for module `stock` --> src/other.rs:1:1 ... create file \"src/other/stock.rs\" ... note: if there is a `mod stock` elsewhere in the crate already, import it with `use crate::...` instead". Writing it twice in the same file gives a 'defined multiple times' error instead.
fix: Replace with: "A second mod stock; somewhere else doesn't reuse the first room: Rust looks for a new file next to that module and stops with E0583, which is what this note warns about."

what: The explanation says the dead_code warning ('field `water` is never read') is true 'since the program never got that far'. That suggests warnings depend on running the program. The warning comes from reading the source: no line of code reads `water`.

fix: "(The warning above it is also true: no line of code ever reads water. The Compiler works that out from the code, without running anything.)"
